name: Arizona
overview: Arizona issues limited big-game permits through three computer draws a year: Pronghorn & Elk (applications due in February), Fall (deer, fall turkey, fall javelina, bighorn sheep, fall bison, sandhill crane; due in June) and Spring (spring turkey, javelina and bison; due in October for the next year's hunts). Applicants list up to five hunt choices per species; up to 20% of each hunt's permits go first to 1st/2nd-choice applicants with the most bonus points, and the rest are drawn at random with one extra random-number entry per bonus point. Nonresidents are limited to 10% of the permits in most hunts, and unissued permits are sold first-come after the draw.

species.drawSystemSummary: Elk permits are drawn in the Pronghorn & Elk (Midwinter) draw. Bonus-point draw: up to 20% of each hunt number's permits are reserved for 1st/2nd-choice applicants with the most bonus points (bonus pass); the rest are drawn at random, first for 1st/2nd choices and then for 3rd-5th choices, with one extra random-number entry per bonus point (including hunter-education and loyalty points).
species.residentNote: A bonus point is earned for an unsuccessful application or by applying with the elk bonus-point-only hunt number (3000); accumulated points are expended when an elk permit-tag is issued in a computer draw.
species.nonresidentNote: Under R12-4-114(E)(2) as printed in the 2026-27 Arizona Hunting Regulations, nonresidents may receive no more than 10% (rounded down) of the permits in any hunt number for antlerless deer, antlerless elk, antlered deer, any deer, any elk, bull elk, javelina, pronghorn, Sandhill crane or turkey. For antlered deer, bull elk, pronghorn, Sandhill crane and turkey hunts with 10 or fewer permits, at most one permit is available to nonresidents, and a one-permit hunt is resident-only. No more than half of the nonresident allotment may be issued in the bonus pass (R12-4-114(G)). The 2025-26 regulations printed the earlier rule, whose 10% cap listed only antlered deer, bull elk, pronghorn, Sandhill crane and turkey hunts.
species.otcSummary: Elk nonpermit-tags (resident $135, nonresident $650) are sold over the counter only for the General or Archery-Only Nonpermit-Tag seasons listed in the elk Commission Order; all other elk hunts require a draw permit.

species.drawSystemSummary: Bighorn sheep permits are drawn in the Fall draw. Up to 20% of all bighorn permits statewide (not per hunt) go to applicants with the most bonus points; the rest are drawn at random with one extra entry per bonus point. Bag limit is one desert and one Rocky Mountain bighorn in a lifetime.
species.residentNote: Applicants who have taken their lifetime bighorn of a subspecies may not apply for that subspecies.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may receive no more than one permit or 10% of all bighorn permits in the draw, whichever is greater, and no more than 50% or more than two of the permits in any hunt number (R12-4-114).
species.otcSummary: None: bighorn sheep require a draw hunt permit-tag.

species.drawSystemSummary: Mountain lion is hunted with an over-the-counter nonpermit-tag (no draw). Bag limit is one lion per calendar year; harvest is managed by zone harvest thresholds.

coverage.notes: Midwinter (Pronghorn & Elk) draws 2023-2026. Counts are from AZGFD draw reports: quota = authorized permits; applicants = 1st-choice applicants (Bonus Pass report); drawn = 1st-choice permits from the bonus pass plus the 1st/2nd-choice pass; odds are drawn/applicants (oddsComputed). byPoints are AZGFD's Bonus Point Report rows (1st+2nd-choice applicants and permits issued in bonus + 1-2 passes, by group bonus points), so they include 2nd-choice draws and do not sum to the 1st-choice totals; the per-point rows also sum to slightly different applicant totals (typically 0-5) than the Bonus Pass report. AZGFD's separate draw-odds summaries (2023-2025) are quoted in each row's note and can differ slightly from the draw-report figures. 2022 draws are not included: AZGFD's 2022 reports list hunt numbers only (hunt numbers are re-assigned each year) and the 2022 Bonus Point Report has rows where totals do not equal resident + nonresident. Draw year = hunt year as labelled by AZGFD.
